retiredUmbrellas.name: StructuralDemandProfile
retiredUmbrellas.reason: too feature-bag-like; replaced by exact ChallengeConditionSpec plus response/recovery relations

retiredUmbrellas.name: FunctionalDifficultyRelation
retiredUmbrellas.reason: too broad as a single named object; retained as a query/projection over smaller relations

retiredUmbrellas.name: SkillChallengeRelation-as-local-derivative
retiredUmbrellas.reason: local sensitivity is useful but only one discrimination projection and fails as complete challenge definition

objects.name: ChallengeConditionSpec
objects.definition: Exact current scope for a challenge query: evaluation commitment/criterion, Game/practice state and rules, horizon, attribution target, control/observation configuration, opponent/other-agent policy or distribution, stochastic/exogenous process, and relevant history/currentness.
objects.guard: configuration metadata, not difficulty by identity

objects.name: CapabilityOutcomeSurface
objects.definition: Conditional distribution of evaluation-relevant outcomes/SRVS as the attribution target's SkillProfile/policy varies under one ChallengeConditionSpec.
objects.guard: surface is not one scalar difficulty and may be multidimensional/nonmonotonic

objects.name: FeasibilityRegion
objects.definition: Region of target profiles/policies/conditions from which the current evaluation criterion is reachable with nonzero admissible support under the declared horizon/action possibilities.
objects.guard: infeasible regions are not maximal challenge

objects.name: CapabilityThresholdRegion
objects.definition: For a declared performance/evaluation criterion, the profile region where criterion satisfaction crosses a declared probability/quality threshold.
objects.analogy: generalizes IRT/Rasch difficulty/location beyond one scalar ability/item and binary outcome
objects.guard: criterion- and scope-relative; not intrinsic Game difficulty

objects.name: CapabilityDiscriminationProfile
objects.definition: How strongly and along which SkillProfile directions outcome distributions change in a declared local/global region of the CapabilityOutcomeSurface.
objects.analogy: generalizes item discrimination/slope; local derivative is one special case
objects.guard: high discrimination is not automatically good PlayerValue, learning value, or fairness

objects.name: SkillIndependentOutcomeComponent
objects.definition: Outcome variation/asymptotes that remain after holding target capability/policy fixed or that are not controllable by that attribution target, including stochastic events, hidden exogenous transitions, or system automation.
objects.guard: not all uncertainty is skill challenge

objects.name: OpponentInteractionSurface
objects.definition: Multi-controller/adversarial extension where relevant outcomes depend jointly on target SkillProfile/policy and opponent/team profiles/policies/distributions.
objects.formalSketch: P(outcome | target profile/policy, opponent/team profile/policy, condition)
objects.guard: opponent strength is not a property of map/content alone

objects.name: ConsequenceRecoveryProfile
objects.definition: Outcome-conditioned authoritative consequences plus routes/costs to continue, recover, retry or redirect pursuit, including time/resource/history/information/social/opportunity dimensions.
objects.guard: changes failure stakes/persistence and participation cost without necessarily changing capability demand

objects.name: FunctionalDifficultyProjection
objects.definition: A query-specific projection over CapabilityOutcomeSurface, FeasibilityRegion, capability threshold/discrimination, skill-independent/opponent components and ConsequenceRecoveryProfile for one attribution/evaluation purpose.
objects.guard: there is no universal projection or scalar without declared purpose/weighting

matchedResults.result: two challenges can have P(success)=0.5 at one profile while one has steep capability discrimination and another is nearly skill-insensitive; equal fail rate does not imply equal skill challenge
two response curves can have equal slope/discrimination but different capability threshold regions; discrimination and difficulty location are independent
same performance/challenge surface with cheap checkpoint versus severe persistent reset yields identical immediate capability demand but different consequence/recovery profile
skill-independent chance can change outcome risk while preserving local skill discrimination/threshold around a region
continuous quality objective can have a non-flat capability-outcome gradient and broad expression challenge with no binary FailureEvent
assistance can shift capability threshold while preserving discrimination, reducing access requirement without erasing skill expression
automation can flatten capability-outcome differences, raising joint performance while reducing Human skill expression/discrimination
assistance can remove one skill dimension while leaving or increasing another, relocating challenge rather than monotonically lowering one scalar
same target profile and map can move from easy to hard as opponent profile changes; challenge surface is relational/multi-agent
same puzzle artifact and rules can shift threshold/discrimination after solution memory/history changes; current history belongs in condition/scope
infeasible zero-support target differs from very-low-probability but capability-sensitive overmatched target
same failure probability can carry radically different time/resource/history costs; probability and consequence severity remain separate

modelTournament.target: binary item success as ability-item relation
modelTournament.survives: location/difficulty and discrimination separation; response function perspective
modelTournament.failsGenerality: usually low-dimensional ability/item, assessment semantics, binary/ordered response assumptions do not cover whole Game challenge
same completion rate can hide different skill sensitivity, action distributions, risk/recovery and population composition

modelTournament.survives: relational skill×task view and learning-specific challenge
modelTournament.failsGenerality: does not by itself cover adversarial, sandbox, stochastic, social, continuous-expression Game challenge

modelTournament.survives: perceived compatibility matters for flow in some contexts
modelTournament.failsGenerality: not a structural difficulty model and balance is not sufficient PlayerValue law

modelTournament.survives: difficulty is controller-relative and mutable; interventions can target performance bands
modelTournament.failsGenerality: matching one performance statistic can change performance without reliably optimizing experience or learning

modelTournament.survives: handles binary/continuous, multidimensional SkillProfile, opponent, assist, stochasticity, history and attribution
modelTournament.openRisk: may still be too abstract; C must test identifiability and minimal measurement requirements

laws: FunctionalDifficulty is a projection, not a primitive scalar
ContinuousChallenge does not require binary FailureEvent
Assistance can shift, flatten, or redirect a capability-outcome surface
Same artifact/rules != same current challenge surface when history, access, opponent, or evaluation commitment changes
MasteryEvidence requires a declared region of the capability-outcome surface, not one peak sample

externalAnchors.pressure: 1PL separates ability and item location/difficulty; 2PL adds discrimination/slope; 3PL adds lower asymptote/guessing, directly pressuring fail-rate=difficulty and sensitivity=whole-challenge collapses

externalAnchors.source: Measuring the level of difficulty in single player video games
externalAnchors.pressure: game difficulty work explicitly links player ability level to conditional probability of losing/completing a challenge; useful precursor to response-surface reconstruction
completion/pass probability alone is limited; action-distribution modeling captures additional level-difficulty structure
adaptive game used multiple difficulty dimensions forming a training space, supporting vector/configuration rather than one difficulty knob
difficulty continuously adapted to skill while flow was not simply a function of absolute skill; Human flow remains a separate outcome
game difficulty and haptic assistance were separately manipulable, supporting assistance as a change in effective capability/access rather than one content-difficulty dimension

N0: response curves separate difficulty/location and discrimination; completion rate is an incomplete descriptor; adaptive systems use multidimensional parameters

foundationReopen.reason: B replaces downstream umbrellas with response/evidence projections over frozen SkillProfile/SRVS/ProbeTransformation and existing Game relations; no semantic foundation law is contradicted.
